questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: The road to the right is one-way only.
There is a detour to the right due to road construction.
The road ahead makes a sharp turn at an extreme angle.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road ahead makes a sharp turn at an extreme angle.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. They tell you about conditions ahead. This sign warns drivers to slow down for a sharp turn.

questions.question: You should yield to a pedestrian:

options.text: Only if they are in a crosswalk.
At all times, even if they are not obeying traffic laws.
Only if the traffic light favors the pedestrian.

questions.correctAnswerText: At all times, even if they are not obeying traffic laws.
questions.explanation: Always watch for pedestrians near your vehicle. You must do everything possible to avoid hitting a pedestrian, no matter what.

questions.question: On a slippery road, you should keep a following distance that is:

options.text: The same as normal.
Longer than normal.
Shorter than normal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Longer than normal.
questions.explanation: Your car needs more distance to stop on a slippery road than on a dry road. Always increase your following distance when roads are slippery.

questions.question: Any amount of alcohol may affect a driver's:

options.text: Right-of-way privileges.
Judgment and physical coordination.
Knowledge.

questions.correctAnswerText: Judgment and physical coordination.
questions.explanation: Any amount of alcohol can harm your ability to drive safely, even small amounts. Alcohol affects judgment and coordination. Driving under the influence can result in criminal charges.

questions.question: Which of the following commonly causes traffic crashes?

options.text: Speeding or driving too fast for conditions.
Getting enough rest and staying alert.
Watching the road and focusing on driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Speeding or driving too fast for conditions.
questions.explanation: Speeding and driving too fast for conditions cause many crashes. Always drive at a safe speed and with the flow of traffic.

questions.question: Using a cell phone while driving is distracting because:

options.text: It makes you worried about the call cost.
It takes your hands, eyes, and attention away from driving.
It gets the attention of other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: It takes your hands, eyes, and attention away from driving.
questions.explanation: Cell phone use while driving is dangerous because it occupies your hands, eyes, and mind. Even skilled drivers increase their crash risk when using a cell phone.

questions.question: When stopped by police for a violation or equipment check, you must show:

options.text: Only your insurance and registration.
Only your license.
Your license, insurance, and registration.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your license, insurance, and registration.
questions.explanation: You must have and show your license, registration, and insurance when stopped. All three documents are required in your vehicle.

questions.question: Night driving is harder because:

options.text: The speed limit is higher at night.
There are fewer cars on the road at night.
It is hard to judge distance and speed in the dark.

questions.correctAnswerText: It is hard to judge distance and speed in the dark.
questions.explanation: At night, reduced visibility makes it difficult to judge distance and how fast other vehicles are traveling. You can only see as far as your headlights reach.

questions.question: If you have a tire blowout, you should:

options.text: Tap or pump the brakes.
Slow down gradually and use light braking.
Apply the brakes hard and fast.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down gradually and use light braking.
questions.explanation: If you have a tire blowout, lift your foot off the accelerator to slow down gradually. Do not brake hard until the vehicle has slowed down.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Drive carefully and be ready to stop.
You must come to a complete stop.
Stop only if needed.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must come to a complete stop.
questions.explanation: A stop sign is the only eight-sided sign on the road. You must come to a complete stop. Do not go until the way is clear to safely cross the intersection.

questions.question: Crashes are more likely when:

options.text: All vehicles travel at about the same speed.
One lane travels faster than other lanes.
One vehicle travels faster or slower than other traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: One vehicle travels faster or slower than other traffic.
questions.explanation: Crashes happen more often when a driver moves faster or slower than other vehicles. Speeding increases crash risk. Driving slower than traffic also increases risk because it can cause rear-end collisions.

questions.question: Motorcycles are entitled to:

options.text: The same full lane width as other vehicles.
The width of the sidewalk.
Half the width of a lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: The same full lane width as other vehicles.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles have the right to use the full lane width, just like all other vehicles.

questions.question: On a wet or icy road, you should:

options.text: Reduce your speed.
Drive at the posted speed.
Speed up.

questions.correctAnswerText: Reduce your speed.
questions.explanation: Your tires grip the road less well when it is wet, snowy, or icy. Slow down on these surfaces.

questions.question: If there is no crosswalk and a pedestrian is crossing your lane, you should:

options.text: Make sure the pedestrian sees you before driving.
Drive carefully around the pedestrian.
Stop and let the pedestrian finish crossing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and let the pedestrian finish crossing.
questions.explanation: You must yield to pedestrians in the road, even without a crosswalk.

questions.question: Distracted driving is:

options.text: Anything that causes you to steer suddenly while driving.
Anything that takes your attention away from driving.
Anything that makes you focus more on driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Anything that takes your attention away from driving.
questions.explanation: Distracted driving is anything that takes your eyes, hands, or mind away from driving. It is the most common cause of reported crashes. Any distraction can cause you to miss warnings and cause a crash.

questions.question: Tailgating (driving too close to another car's bumper):

options.text: Can make other drivers angry and frustrated.
Cannot result in a traffic ticket.
Prevents other cars from cutting in front of you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can make other drivers angry and frustrated.
questions.explanation: Tailgating is dangerous and can cause aggressive driving. Drivers can get tickets for unsafe driving.

questions.question: Which driving skills are affected by alcohol and/or drugs?

options.text: Alertness.
Coordination.
Both of these.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both of these.
questions.explanation: Alcohol and drugs hurt many driving skills. They slow your reaction time, hurt your coordination, reduce alertness, and make it hard to concentrate.

questions.question: At a crosswalk:

options.text: You must let pedestrians cross first.
Pedestrians must let you go first.
Construction workers have the right of way.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must let pedestrians cross first.
questions.explanation: Pedestrians have the right of way at crosswalks. You must stop for pedestrians in a crosswalk, whether it is marked or unmarked. Pedestrians must follow traffic signals.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Stop sign.
Regulatory sign.
School zone or school crossing sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: School zone or school crossing sign.
questions.explanation: Five-sided signs alert drivers to school zones. They warn that children or other pedestrians may be crossing the road nearby.

questions.question: Blind spots are:

options.text: Areas where your vision blurs when you are tired.
Parts of the road you cannot see in your mirrors.
Road signs and signals.

questions.correctAnswerText: Parts of the road you cannot see in your mirrors.
questions.explanation: When changing lanes, look over your shoulder in the direction you want to move. Check for vehicles near the rear corners of your car. These hidden areas are called blind spots.

questions.question: When passing another vehicle:

options.text: Pass it as slowly as possible.
Drive at the same speed as the car you are passing.
Pass it as safely and quickly as possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pass it as safely and quickly as possible.
questions.explanation: Pass quickly and safely so you can see clearly. Return to your lane only when you see both headlights of the other car in your mirror.

questions.question: A green traffic light means you should:

options.text: Stop completely.
Speed up to quickly cross the intersection.
Go straight, turn left, or turn right as allowed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Go straight, turn left, or turn right as allowed.
questions.explanation: A green light means you can go straight or turn. When turning, first yield to pedestrians and other cars in the intersection.

questions.question: You are driving behind a large truck on the freeway. You should drive:

options.text: Closer behind it than you would a regular car.
Farther behind it than you would a regular car.
To the right side of the truck and wait to pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Farther behind it than you would a regular car.
questions.explanation: Stay farther back from large trucks because they have larger blind spots and it is harder to see around them.

questions.question: When you see a flashing yellow light at an intersection, you must:

options.text: Come to a complete stop.
Keep driving at your normal speed.
Slow down and drive carefully.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and drive carefully.
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light means be alert and proceed carefully. Slow down when you approach a flashing yellow light.

questions.question: When turning left at an intersection:

options.text: You must yield to oncoming cars and pedestrians.
Oncoming cars and pedestrians must yield to you.
You never need to yield to oncoming cars or pedestrians.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must yield to oncoming cars and pedestrians.
questions.explanation: When turning left, you must yield to oncoming traffic. You must always yield to pedestrians.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: The road ends ahead.
The road splits and you must go either right or left.
A four-way intersection is ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road splits and you must go either right or left.
questions.explanation: This yellow warning sign shows a fork in the road. You must choose to go either right or left.

questions.question: There is no crosswalk and you see a pedestrian crossing in front of you. You should:

options.text: Make eye contact and then pass the pedestrian.
Slow down while passing the pedestrian.
Stop and let the pedestrian finish crossing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and let the pedestrian finish crossing.
questions.explanation: You must yield to pedestrians at any crosswalk, marked or unmarked. Always stop for pedestrians crossing, even without a crosswalk.

questions.question: To keep your tires from losing grip on wet roads, you should:

options.text: Make sharp turns.
Press hard on the brakes.
Slow down.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down.
questions.explanation: Slow down on wet roads to prevent loss of grip. Keep your tires in good condition. If you lose control, release the gas, do not brake, stay steady, and let the car slow down naturally.

questions.question: Backing up your vehicle is:

options.text: Always dangerous.
Dangerous only if you have a helper.
Only dangerous in large trucks.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always dangerous.
questions.explanation: Backing up is always dangerous because you cannot see well behind your car. Always be extra careful when backing up.

questions.question: At a railroad crossing, you must:

options.text: Watch for vehicles that must always stop (school buses, trucks with hazardous materials, etc.).
Watch for trains coming from either direction.
Both of these.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both of these.
questions.explanation: Approach all railroad crossings with extreme caution. Cross only when you are sure no train is coming from either direction. Watch for school buses and hazardous material trucks that must stop at all crossings.
